description: NaBi₃V₂O₁₀ crystallizes in the triclinic P1 space group. Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.43-2.70 Å. There are two inequivalent V sites. In the first V site, V is bonded to four O atoms to form VO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one BiO₅ square pyramid. There are a spread of V-O bond distances ranging from 1.71-1.78 Å. In the second V site, V is bonded to four O atoms to form VO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent BiO₅ square pyramids. There are a spread of V-O bond distances ranging from 1.69-1.79 Å. There are three inequivalent Bi sites. In the first Bi site, Bi is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Bi-O bond distances ranging from 2.17-2.44 Å. In the second Bi site, Bi is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted BiO₅ square pyramids that share corners with three VO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Bi-O bond distances ranging from 2.20-2.40 Å. In the third Bi site, Bi is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Bi-O bond distances ranging from 2.28-2.80 Å. There are ten inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to one Na and three Bi atoms to form edge-sharing ONaBi₃ tetrahedra. In the second O site, O is bonded to one Na and three Bi atoms to form edge-sharing ONaBi₃ tetrahedra. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal non-coplanar geometry to one Na, one V, and one Bi atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 1-coordinate geometry to one V and two Bi atoms. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one V and two Bi atoms. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one V, and one Bi atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one V and two Bi atoms. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one V, and one Bi atom. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Na and one V atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one V and one Bi atom.
